svg.title: Localized quantum light source in a 1H-WSe₂ monolayer
svg.desc: A ball-and-stick model of one trigonal-prismatic Se–W–Se monolayer. The top and bottom selenium atoms share in-plane coordinates. A localized quantum-dot-like emitter is marked by a small amber glow; one symbolic light path extends normal to the plane.
svg.metadata: Original drawing. Geometry: Fang et al., Physical Review B 92, 205108 (2015), Fig. 1 and Table I, https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.92.205108. Monolayer lattice parameter a=3.32 angstroms; Se plane separation 3.35 angstroms. Coordinates: W at R; Se at R+(u+v)/3 with z=+1.675 and -1.675 angstroms, using a 60-degree hexagonal basis. Nearest-neighbor W–Se distances are 2.5455 angstroms. Clipping an ideal sheet creates finite edges. Sphere sizes and the optical overlay are illustrative. The localized optical state and layer-normal light path are conceptual. The drawing does not model a specific confinement mechanism or angular radiation pattern. Background on localized emitters: https://doi.org/10.1038/nnano.2015.75.
